reviewed_content: The final eight-page set is consistent with actual preview 004: seven pages are byte-identical; SOURCE_INDEX alone adds the documented 39 precise references. No gameplay or page-content deviation from the reviewed candidate was found.

The formal binding map and weapon reverse indexes resolve exactly two implementations and three actual marks: Galvanic Rifle Branx Mk CV, Quickdraw Stub Revolver Zarona Mk IIa, and Quickdraw Stub Revolver Agripinaa Mk XIV.

Tier/wrapper values agree: each qualifying shot adds one effective ranged-power layer at I–IV .045/.05/.055/.06, maximum five effective layers; child offset accounts for the raw placeholder. The same-key child override replaces the fallback rather than adding an extra bonus.

Only the actual hip/aim hitscan shot emits the aggregate weakspot on_shoot condition; one shot is at most one layer regardless of targets. Melee sweeps, push, reload/aim/flashlight controls and weapon switching do not trigger or consume ranged power. Damage resolves before the queued proc and later cache rebuild, so the triggering shot does not retroactively use its layer.

The 3.5-second shared timer refreshes on a qualifying weakspot event even at cap; non-weakspot or miss events neither clear nor refresh it. Holstering continues the timer while the held-slot gate removes the stat from use; true unequip/removal destroys the parent and children.

The controlled example 4→5 layers gives 124→130 for normalized curve-output input 100 at tier IV: +6 percentage points, +6 normalized units, and about 4.84% relative to 124; it is explicitly not a final-HP percentage. The separate cap-refresh example is consistent with the shared timer behavior.
